title: Urinary Tract Agents: Nitrofurantoin, Fosfomycin, Methenamine

questions.question: Regarding intravenous fosfomycin:

parts.text: List three approved indications by Health Canada.
What is the mechanism of action of fosfomycin?
Name one Enterobacterales that is intrinsically resistant to fosfomycin.

parts_raw.text: List THREE approved indications by Health Canada.
What is the mechanism of action of fosfomycin?
Name ONE Enterobacterales that is intrinsically resistant to fosfomycin.

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Complicated urinary tract infection including acute pyelonephritis (2) Nosocomial/hospital-acquired pneumonia (3) Complicated skin and soft-tissue infection (bacteraemia associated with these and bone/joint infection are also listed). b) Fosfomycin is bactericidal and blocks the first step of bacterial cell-wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis by inhibiting MurA (UDP-N-acetylglucosamine enolpyruvyl transferase), preventing formation of N-acetylmuramic acid; it enters the cell via the glycerophosphate and hexose-phosphate transport systems. c) Morganella morganii.
questions.beyond_mandell: IV fosfomycin Health Canada (Fomicyt) indications and the intrinsic resistance of Morganella morganii are from the product monograph/EUCAST, not this oral-focused chapter, which cites only the mechanism.

parts_raw.text: Name 3 Health Canada-approved indications for IV fosfomycin (1.5)
What is the major mechanism for fosfomycin (0.5)
Name one Enterobacterales species that is intrinsically resistant to fosfomycin (0.5)

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Complicated urinary tract infection including acute pyelonephritis (2) Nosocomial/hospital-acquired pneumonia (3) Complicated skin and soft-tissue infection (also bacteraemia associated with these indications and bone/joint infection). b) Inhibits the first committed step of peptidoglycan (cell-wall) synthesis by blocking MurA (enolpyruvyl transferase), which uses phosphoenolpyruvate; the drug is taken up via glycerophosphate and hexose-phosphate transporters. c) Morganella morganii.
questions.beyond_mandell: IV fosfomycin Health Canada indications and Morganella morganii intrinsic resistance come from the product monograph/EUCAST; the chapter supports only the cell-wall/peptidoglycan mechanism.

cohort_answer.text: Indications: Complicated UTI/pyelonephritis; Nosocomial pneumonia; Osteomyelitis; Bacterial meningitis; Skin and soft tissue infection; Bacteremia related to above indications. Mechanism: Interferes with cell wall synthesis - inhibits phosphoenolpyruvate synthetase, blocking formation of N-acetylmuramic acid, ultimately interfering with early cell wall synthesis (Mandell's). Intrinsically resistant species: Morganella morganii

questions.question: From the antibiotics Amikacin, Azithromycin, Clindamycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, Ertapenem, Linezolid, Levofloxacin, and Nitrofurantoin (each used only once), match each side effect to one antibiotic.
questions.question_raw: Given list of antibiotics and side effects (Amikacin, Azithromycin, Clindamycin, Pip/Tazo, Ertapenem, Linezolid, Levofloxacin, Nitrofurantoin), and antibiotics can only be used once, match each side effect to an antibiotic:

parts.text: Isolated thrombocytopenia | Isolated neutropenia | Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis | Peripheral neuropathy | Tendinopathy

parts_raw.text: Isolated thrombocytopenia | Isolated neutropenia | Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis | Peripheral neuropathy | Tendonopathy

questions.model_answer: Isolated thrombocytopenia - piperacillin-tazobactam; Isolated neutropenia - azithromycin; Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (chronic pulmonary reaction) - nitrofurantoin; Peripheral neuropathy - linezolid; Tendinopathy/tendon rupture - levofloxacin. (Note: linezolid characteristically causes thrombocytopenia as well, but with each drug used once it is assigned here to the peripheral neuropathy it also produces via mitochondrial toxicity.)
questions.beyond_mandell: Nitrofurantoin pulmonary toxicity, fluoroquinolone tendinopathy, and beta-lactam/macrolide cytopenias are not covered in this Mandell chapter; standard drug-toxicity knowledge.

cohort_answer.text: Isolated thrombocytopenia - piptazo. Isolated neutropenia - azithromycin. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis - nitrofurantoin. Peripheral neuropathy - linezolid. Tendonopathy - levofloxacin

questions.question: Complete the intrinsic-resistance table for Morganella, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae against nitrofurantoin, cephalexin, fosfomycin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate.
questions.question_raw: 8. Antimicrobial intrinsic resistance. Table: | Nitrofurantoin | Cephalexin | Fosfomycin | Amox-Clav for Morganella, Proteus mirabilis, E. cloacae

parts.text: Fill out the intrinsic resistance table.

parts_raw.text: Fill out the intrinsic resistance table

questions.model_answer:
Morganella morganii: nitrofurantoin R; cephalexin R; fosfomycin no reliable breakpoint/unreliable; amoxicillin-clavulanate R.
Proteus mirabilis: nitrofurantoin R; cephalexin susceptible (not intrinsically resistant); fosfomycin no reliable breakpoint/unreliable; amoxicillin-clavulanate susceptible (not intrinsically resistant).
Enterobacter cloacae: nitrofurantoin variable (+/-); cephalexin R (AmpC); fosfomycin no reliable breakpoint/unreliable; amoxicillin-clavulanate R (AmpC).
questions.beyond_mandell: Intrinsic-resistance assignments are from CLSI M100 intrinsic-resistance tables; this chapter notes E. cloacae AmpC and that Morganella/Proteus are lactose-negative but does not tabulate these agents.

cohort_answer.text: Morganella: Nitrofurantoin R, Cephalexin R, Fosfomycin unreliable/no breakpoints, Amox-Clav R. Proteus mirabilis: Nitrofurantoin R, Cephalexin None (susceptible), Fosfomycin unreliable/no breakpoints, Amox-Clav None (susceptible). E. cloacae: Nitrofurantoin +/-, Cephalexin R, Fosfomycin unreliable/no breakpoints, Amox-Clav R

questions.question: Name three antibiotics with gram-negative coverage to which Proteus and Providencia are intrinsically resistant.

parts.text: Name three antibiotics with gram-negative coverage that are intrinsically resistant to Proteus and Providencia.

parts_raw.text: Name three antibiotics with gram negative coverage that are intrinsically resistant to proteus and providencia

questions.model_answer: (1) Nitrofurantoin (2) Polymyxins (colistin/polymyxin B) (3) Tigecycline. (Proteus spp. and Providencia spp. are intrinsically resistant to all three despite their general gram-negative activity.)
questions.beyond_mandell: Intrinsic-resistance patterns per EUCAST Expert Rules / CLSI; the chapter notes Proteus resists methenamine via urease-driven alkaline urine but does not tabulate this list.

questions.question: Complete the intrinsic-resistance table (resistant: Yes/No) for Fosfomycin, Nitrofurantoin, Amoxicillin-clavulanate, and Cephalexin against Enterobacter, Morganella, and Proteus mirabilis.
questions.question_raw: Q32 (2015) Intrinsic Mechanism of Resistance. Fill in table of organisms with intrinsic resistance: | Fosfomycin | Nitrofurantoin | Amox/Clav | Cephalexin for Enterobacter, Morganella, Proteus mirabilis

parts.text: Fill in the intrinsic resistance table.

parts_raw.text: Fill in the intrinsic resistance table

questions.model_answer: Enterobacter | Fosfomycin: No | Nitrofurantoin: No | Amox/clav: Yes | Cephalexin: Yes (intrinsic AmpC confers resistance to aminopenicillin/BLI combinations and first-generation cephalosporins). Morganella morganii | Fosfomycin: Yes | Nitrofurantoin: Yes | Amox/clav: Yes | Cephalexin: Yes (intrinsically resistant to all four). Proteus mirabilis | Fosfomycin: No | Nitrofurantoin: Yes | Amox/clav: No | Cephalexin: No (intrinsic nitrofurantoin resistance; retains susceptibility to fosfomycin, amox/clav, and 1st-gen cephalosporins).
questions.beyond_mandell: Intrinsic-resistance grid follows EUCAST/CLSI intrinsic-resistance tables; this chapter notes Enterobacter/Serratia inducible AmpC but does not tabulate these agents.

cohort_answer.text: Enterobacter | No | No | Yes | Yes. Morganella | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes. Proteus mirabilis | No | Yes | No | No.
